title:
I'm a beginner learning embedded C on an STM32 NUCLEO-F446RE board (STM32F446RE chip), using STM32CubeIDE 2.x and STM32CubeMX with the HAL library (STM32Cube FW_F4 V1.28.3). This folder is my CubeMX-generated STM32CubeIDE project.

Goal: pressing the blue user button B1 (PC13, active-low, board has an external pull-up) should trigger an EXTI interrupt on the falling edge. The interrupt sets a volatile flag. The main loop sees the flag, increments a counter, prints "Pressed N\r\n" over USART2 (PA2/PA3, 115200 baud, the ST-LINK virtual COM port, which shows up on my Mac as /dev/tty.usbmodem103), and toggles the green LED LD2 (PA5).

Problem: after flashing and opening `screen /dev/tty.usbmodem103 115200`, I don't see any "Pressed" messages when I press the button. Before switching to interrupts, a polling version of this code worked (printing and LED toggling were fine).

What I changed:
- In CubeMX: PC13 set to GPIO_EXTI13, falling edge, no pull. I did NOT regenerate after enabling NVIC, so I added the NVIC setup by hand.
- Core/Src/main.c: global `volatile uint8_t button_pressed`; `HAL_NVIC_SetPriority(EXTI15_10_IRQn, 0, 0)` and `HAL_NVIC_EnableIRQ(EXTI15_10_IRQn)` in USER CODE BEGIN MX_GPIO_Init_2; `HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback` in USER CODE BEGIN 4 that sets the flag when GPIO_Pin == B1_Pin; main loop checks the flag and prints/toggles.
- Core/Src/stm32f4xx_it.c: added `EXTI15_10_IRQHandler` in USER CODE BEGIN 1 that calls `HAL_GPIO_EXTI_IRQHandler(B1_Pin)`.
- I recently removed an accidental duplicate EXTI15_10_IRQHandler that I had placed inside main().

Please:
1. Read Core/Src/main.c, Core/Src/stm32f4xx_it.c, Core/Inc/main.h, and the .ioc file, and find anything that would stop the interrupt, the callback, the UART print, or the LED toggle from working.
2. If possible, build the project from the command line to check for compile or link errors (for example with the makefile in the Debug folder if it exists, using arm-none-eabi-gcc).
3. Fix the problem. Rules:
   - Only edit code between /* USER CODE BEGIN */ and /* USER CODE END */ markers, so CubeMX regeneration won't erase it.
   - Do not edit the startup file (startup_stm32f446xx.s).
   - Do not regenerate the project with CubeMX.
4. You can't see the board. If you need information only the hardware can give (does the LED react, what the debugger shows, what Terminal prints), tell me exactly what to check and what each result would mean.
5. Explain what was wrong and what you changed in simple language, as if teaching a beginner. Define any term you use.
